scenes.caption: Which card should I use? A $100.00 cart at Sample Kitchen, a fictional store; your cards: Double Cash, Quicksilver, Freedom Unlimited, Blue Cash Everyday.

Your best card, right on your cart. The badge: Use Double Cash · $2.00 back, the highest guaranteed estimate. Its panel: based on $100.00 cart estimated total at Sample Kitchen, treated as a restaurant; Double Cash $2.00, 2% if the balance is paid.

The rule, in the issuer’s words. Then Quicksilver $1.50; Freedom Unlimited $1.50–$3.00 if its conditions are met: 3% on “dining at restaurants, including takeout and eligible delivery services”, with no spend limit stated by the issuer, otherwise 1.5%; Blue Cash Everyday $1.00.
Amounts only when certain. A gift card is applied, so the cart amount isn’t read; the badge ranks your cards by rate: Blue Cash Everyday 3%, Double Cash 2%, Quicksilver 1.5%, Freedom Unlimited 1.5%.

Card terms kept current by an LLM; every change approved by a person: issuer terms, an LLM drafts, a person approves, your extension (177 cards; checks for updates weekly). No model at checkout: the comparison is arithmetic on your device. Your cards are saved in your browser; no card numbers, no bank login. Usage reports only if you choose Share; tapping Suggest or Report sends the store’s domain.
AI Checkout. The best card you already own, shown right on your cart. Works at any U.S. online store. Illustration with sample cards and a fictional store.

limits: Illustration, not a recording: simplified recreations of the 2.1.0 badge and panels.
Sample cards; Sample Kitchen (sample-kitchen.example) and shop.example.com are fictional stores.
Amounts are conditional estimates from published terms, not earned rewards.
Same inputs give the same frames on the same machine and browser build; byte parity across operating systems, font rasterizers or encoders is not claimed.
